title: fix(service-storage)!: the chunked completion assembles the parts the upload holds, and a re-sent chunk is counted once (#22313)
body:
Fixes #22313
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## Summary

A chunked upload now completes with the file it was sent, or not at all.

- **The completion door** (`POST /storage/upload/chunked/:uploadId/complete`) assembles the upload's own record of the chunks it holds: every chunk the chunk door stored, with the eTag the backend answered for it. It no longer assembles the request's `parts` list. The list is checked against the record, and the record is checked against the declared `totalChunks` / `totalSize`. When any check fails, the door answers **`409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`** before anything is assembled. `error.details` names the chunk indexes: `missingChunks`, `unexpectedChunks`, `unheldListedChunks` and `mismatchedChunks`, plus `totalChunks`, `totalSize` and `heldBytes`. The session stays `in_progress` and the file stays `pending`, so the uploader can send what is missing and complete again.
- **The chunk door** (`PUT …/chunk/:chunkIndex`): a re-sent index replaces its slot in `sys_upload_session.parts`. `uploaded_chunks` counts distinct chunks. `uploaded_size` is the sum of each chunk's latest size, which uses the per-part size PR #22311 records. A session whose record predates those sizes keeps its running total, as PR #22311 judges it.
- **`packages/client` is unchanged.** Because the door completes from the stored parts, the SDK's `resumeUpload` is correct as it is: it lists only the parts its own pass sent. The pins below drive the doors in exactly that order.

## Measured: before (main `4e4111ca`) and after

The pins were committed first (`ab583f369d`, `4508df0ec0`) and run on unfixed main before `storage-routes.ts` was touched.

| Pin | main `4e4111ca` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Resumed 2-chunk upload (chunk 0 = 5 MiB stored in a first pass; the resume sends chunk 1 = 10 B and completes listing only chunk 1) | `200`, `size` 5242890, stored object **10 bytes** (unit and over HTTP) | `200`, stored object 5242890 bytes, byte-equal to chunk0 + chunk1 (unit, and read back through `GET /storage/files/:id/url` over HTTP) |
| Upload that never received chunk 0, completed | `200` | `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `details.missingChunks` = `[0]`; session `in_progress`; the backend assembly is not called |
| Chunk 0 (600 KiB) of a 1 MiB session sent twice, then progress read | `uploadedSize` 1228800, `uploadedChunks` 2, `percentComplete` 100 | 614400 / 1 / 59, identical to the reading after one send |
| CONTROL: a clean one-pass upload listing every part | `200`, full file | `200`, full file (unchanged) |

## Why the door completes from stored parts rather than refusing every short list (dispatch H2 / H4)

Two measurements decided this.

- **The server holds what assembly needs.** The record stores, for every chunk, the eTag the backend itself answered at upload time. S3's `CompleteMultipartUpload` needs part numbers and those eTags; the local adapter reads part files by number and ignores eTags. So the server can fill any part the request omits.
- **The client cannot list what the record holds.** The progress answer (`UploadProgressSchema`) carries no parts or eTags, so `resumeUpload` cannot list the parts an earlier pass sent. Exposing them would be a `packages/spec` change, which is fenced. Refusing every list that omits a stored part would therefore refuse every real SDK resume.

Assembling the record still refuses a short assembly. The door refuses any upload whose record lacks a declared chunk or does not add up to the declared size. Triage's pin is "completes with the full file or is refused", and both halves hold.

## Files outside the dispatch's file list (a declared fence deviation)

- `packages/plugins/organizations/src/storage-upload-door-ownership.wall.test.ts` and `storage-upload-organization-change.wall.test.ts`: three POSITIVE legs (one, plus two) completed a 10-byte chunked upload that held none of its bytes and expected `200`. That `200` is this defect, and the door now refuses it. Each leg now sends the declared 10 bytes as chunk 0 before completing. The refusals these files pin (ownership `403`, organization-change `409`) run before the new check and are unchanged.
- In `service-storage`, five existing tests did the same zero-byte completion and were updated the same way. `tenant-audit-update-delete-half-repairs.test.ts`'s recording engine double now applies a by-id `update` to its row, as the real engine does. Without that, the completion could not read back the record the chunk door wrote.

## Tests, ablation and gates (final union at `0342e008b0`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 45 files / **749 passed**, including 13 in the new `src/chunked-upload-integrity.test.ts`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage typecheck` (tsc, scripts and test layer): exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/organizations exec vitest run` on the two wall files: **20 passed**. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/organizations typecheck`: exit 0 (at `b0b1ca0d83`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run --project isolated` on `test/storage-chunked-resume-integrity.dogfood.test.ts` and PR #22311's `test/storage-upload-limits.dogfood.test.ts`: **6 passed**. The new dogfood file compiles with 0 errors in `tsc --noEmit --listFiles`. The package-wide dogfood typecheck was NOT MEASURED locally: 84 TS2307 errors come from packages not built in this tree, none in this diff.
- **Ablation** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, wrap mode; each leg's mutation and restore were proven by blob hash against HEAD). The unit suite imports `./storage-routes.js` from source, so no dist was involved.
  - A1, assemble the request's list instead of the record: the resumed-upload pin and 3 others go red.
  - A2, refusal disarmed: all 7 refusal pins go red. The first A2 leg was a no-op that the tool refused (its replacement was a substring of the anchor); it was re-run with a distinct replacement.
  - A2b, eTag check removed: only the mismatched-eTag pin goes red.
  - A2c, size check removed: the size and legacy-total pins go red.
  - A3, running total kept: the re-sent-progress pin goes red.
  - A4, append instead of replace: the re-sent-progress and replace-slot pins go red.
  - The dogfood file's red leg is its run on main above.
- Gates at `0342e008b0`: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 72 families (unchanged after the last merge). All 72 were run, plus `pnpm check:error-status-conformance` by hand, and every one exited 0. The error-status gate printed "every derivable runtime status is documented, and every documented status is reachable". `pnpm check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` printed OK, `pnpm check:engine-double-contract` printed OK with 983 pinned, and `--ran` reconciled 72 of 72. (In the first run, before the last merge, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` exited 3 with PREREQUISITE NOT MET because this tree was not fully built. Both were measured green in this run.)
- Lint: `eslint --no-inline-config` on the 9 touched `.ts` files reported 9 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings (JSON count). `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.

## Acceptance notes

- **Concurrent chunk PUTs lose a record entry (an existing defect, reported to the seat rather than fixed here).** The chunk door reads, modifies and writes `parts`. Two concurrent PUTs (chunks 0 and 1) both answered `200`, and the record kept only chunk 0. With this change, that upload's completion is refused `409` with `missingChunks` = `[1]`, so re-sending chunk 1 finishes it. On main, the same race corrupted the progress silently. No in-repo client uploads chunks in parallel: the SDK's `resumeUpload` is sequential, and objectui uses the presigned flow.
- A resumed upload with a hole that is not a prefix (chunk 1 held, chunk 0 not) gets a `409` naming chunk 0 from the SDK, because `resumeUpload` resumes from the `uploadedChunks` count. The refusal's `details.missingChunks` is enough for a client to resume exactly; teaching the SDK to read it is a separate client change.
- The chunk door still accepts a chunk index at or beyond `totalChunks`. The completion now refuses such an upload (`unexpectedChunks`), so no extra bytes reach an assembled file.
- A `parts` value that is not a list of `{ chunkIndex, eTag }` is now refused `400 INVALID_REQUEST`. It used to throw a `500`. An absent `parts` is still an empty list.
